candidates.title: OPENFERMENT_HOST in the installing shell installs a server on every interface, and guard.py admits writes from any machine on the network
candidates.statement: install.sh takes OPENFERMENT_HOST from the environment and writes it into the server's LaunchDaemon, so OPENFERMENT_HOST=0.0.0.0 installs a service listening on every interface with one line of notice, and guard.refusal allows a POST that names the Mini's LAN address in Host.
candidates.contract: CLAUDE.md:52 "R: The service binds `127.0.0.1`; the loopback bind and `core/openferment_core/guard.py` are the access control until accounts exist"; CLAUDE.md:137 stop condition "Widening network exposure ... the service keeps its loopback bind"; docs/runbooks/live-host-install.md:146 "The service binds `127.0.0.1` and nothing else"
candidates.expected: The installed server job listens on 127.0.0.1, or install.sh stops and asks before it writes a wider address.
candidates.observed: install.sh exit 0; its one line on the address: "The server listens on 0.0.0.0:8000 (OPENFERMENT_HOST), so Tailscale is left alone."; the plist's ProgramArguments hold --host 0.0.0.0; guard.refusal('POST', {host: '192.168.1.20:8000'}) and {host: 'mini.local:8000'} both answer allowed. Reads stay open by guard.py's own rule, so Guild's personnel ledger is readable from the LAN too.
candidates.cause: scripts/host/lib.sh:41 HOST="${OPENFERMENT_HOST:-127.0.0.1}" reaches launchd.py --host (install.sh:81); launchd.py:57-62 checks the paths, user and port and takes any host; guard.py answers_to admits every IP address and .local name and checks no peer address. The runbook names no OPENFERMENT_HOST.
candidates.evidence: wide-bind.sh runs install.sh once on stand-ins (standins.sh: uname, id, brew, sudo, launchctl, pmset, plutil, tailscale, curl, pnpm, uv and the keg's PostgreSQL tools, each logging its call) with OPENFERMENT_HOST=0.0.0.0, reads the written plist with plistlib and calls guard.refusal in the repo's Python. The knob is deliberate in lib.sh's comments; the finding is that it widens the bind against the R line with no ask.

needsLiveModel: What the Postdoc screen and the nightly's extraction and brief steps say when the example's placeholder key (H11-01) meets Anthropic's answer to it: the calls themselves are the model door, so they were never made here.
held: install.sh run twice on stand-ins, from a checkout path and a HOME each holding a space: the daemons folder, the jobs launchd holds, core/.env (one database line, mode 600) and HOME are the same after both runs; the second run makes no database and writes no line (install-twice.sh).

backup_database's rotation at seven and eight files, night by night across 31 October into November and 31 December into 2027, the same night twice, a dump failing half way, a dump onto a full disk (/dev/full), other files in the folder, folder 700 and dumps 600, all under a HOME with a space (backup-rotation.sh, also with BASH_COMPAT=32).

The night's dump with the real pg_dump (16.15) and the runbook's step 7 restore with the real createdb and pg_restore, on test databases: 44 tables, every row count equal; the one pg_restore error is COMMENT ON EXTENSION vector for a non-superuser role, which the Mini's Homebrew superuser does not meet (dump-restore.sh).

env_setting against python-dotenv over 645 forms of the line: every difference is an unclosed quote (the comment's third named form), a `\n` escape inside double quotes, or a later bare name (env_setting_fuzz.py).

ShellCheck 0.11.0 at style severity with every optional check on install.sh, deploy.sh, nightly.sh, lib.sh, session-start.sh and engines-local.sh: nothing at the default checks; with -o all, only brace, [[ ]], masked-status and default-case notes.

deploy.sh's refusals and paths on stand-ins: an unknown option, two dirty files named on one line, a modified biorepo.json with and without a database named, a rebase left half-done, --no-pull --no-restart, no job installed; --verify names the tests' server from core/.env, from the live address (openferment_test on its server, a query dropped), or as the user on 127.0.0.1, with UV_FROZEN=1 (deploy-cases.sh).

nightly.sh as launchd runs it (env -i, /bin/bash, HOME with a space): the dump first, the extraction only with a project named, a failed step makes exit 1 and the others still run, an `export NAME="x" # c` line read as python-dotenv reads it (nightly-cases.sh).
lib.sh's poll_host and launchd.poll_host agree on loopback, everywhere, IPv4, IPv6 and bracketed inputs; launchd.py --read reads back host and port, and refuses a missing or broken plist with exit 1.

Every command, flag and path the runbook names exists in the tree: the pnpm scripts (ready, db:migrate, db:import-alpha1 with --name, --by and --data, geneos:fetch, build, prove, verify's sixteen stages), conform with --inputs and --project, write_placeholder_inputs(path, by=), the ready rows by name, LIVE_START, the extras sim, lit, agent and dev, packageManager pnpm@10.33.0, the clone address, the alpha-1.0 and alpha-2.1 commits, alpha 1.0's install.sh --uninstall with the same two labels, biorepo.json unchanged between alpha 1.0 and 2047f5a, hash routing for #/p/<id>.

No host script prints, logs or passes on the key: has_key greps quietly, session-start writes it with printf under umask 177 and checks git ignores the file, and the plists carry PATH, HOME and PYTHONUNBUFFERED alone.

unexamined.item: Running any host script on macOS's /bin/bash 3.2 and BSD userland
unexamined.reason: The container is Linux with bash 5.2 and GNU tools; building bash 3.2.57 here was refused by the sandbox. Every bash 3.2 and BSD point was reasoned against the man pages and marked read: process substitution, here-strings, ${!name:-}, [[:space:]] classes in patterns, tail -1 and -n +8, paste -sd: -, mktemp -d, date +%F, cut, tr, sort -r with LC_ALL=C all hold; no associative arrays, mapfile, ${var,,}, &>>, local -n, printf -v, negative offsets, sed -i, readlink -f or stat in the host scripts.

unexamined.item: launchd's own behaviour (log files' owner, ExitTimeOut, StartCalendarInterval after sleep), Homebrew's brew services --sudo-service-user, fdesetup, pmset, plutil and Tailscale's CLI
unexamined.reason: macOS and its tools are absent here; each was stood in for and its use read.
